## Project Overview

- This repository appears to be Lodash, a JavaScript utility library distributed for browser and Node.js use. Its package metadata identifies the project as `lodash` version `4.18.1`, while the README documents browser `<script>` usage, npm installation, and Node.js imports. [package.json][README.md:34-64]
- The main implementation is the generated `lodash.js` file, which exposes collection, array, object, string, function, and utility operations such as `map`, `reduce`, `cloneDeep`, `isEqual`, and `template`. [lodash.js:9651-9654][lodash.js:9776-9781][lodash.js:11186-11188][lodash.js:11630-11632][lodash.js:14886-14920]
- The visible technologies include JavaScript, Node.js, npm, Bun, Webpack, QUnit, Playwright, Markdown documentation tooling, and CodeQL JavaScript analysis. [package.json][.github/workflows/ci-bun.yml][.github/workflows/browser-testing.yml][.github/workflows/codeql.yml]
- Likely entry points for consumers are `lodash.js`, the Node.js package imports documented in the README, and the generated `dist/` builds. [README.md:34-64][test/fp.html:10-18]
- The repository also contains build and documentation generators for the main library and its functional-programming variant. [lib/main/build-dist.js:24-29][lib/fp/build-dist.js:48-54][lib/main/build-doc.js:76-81][lib/fp/build-doc.js:73-76]

## Setup / Installation

- Node.js is a prerequisite; the package declares support for Node.js `>=4.0.0`. [package.json]
- npm is the primary documented package manager: the README shows installing Lodash with `npm i --save lodash`, and the CI workflows install dependencies with `npm install`. [README.md:34-64][.github/workflows/ci-docs.yml][.github/workflows/ci-node.yml]
- Bun is also supported by a CI workflow, which runs `bun install` and `bun run validate` across Bun versions `1.0.0`, `1.1.0`, `1.2.0`, and `1.3.0`. [.github/workflows/ci-bun.yml]
- A basic setup is to install the repository dependencies with `npm install`. [.github/workflows/ci-docs.yml]
- Browser-test setup additionally installs Playwright browsers and dependencies with `npx playwright install --with-deps`, then installs `@playwright/test` as a development dependency. [.github/workflows/browser-testing.yml]
- The supplied evidence does not show any required application environment variables or an environment-file setup. [package.json][.github/workflows/ci-docs.yml]
- The README also documents using the browser build directly with `<script src="lodash.js"></script>`. [README.md:34-38]

## Running Locally

- Build the complete project with `npm run build`; this runs both the main and FP distribution builds. [package.json]
- Build only the main distribution with `npm run build:main`, or build only the FP distribution with `npm run build:fp`. [package.json]
- Build generated module files with `npm run build:main-modules` and `npm run build:fp-modules`. [package.json]
- Generate documentation with `npm run doc:fp`, `npm run doc:site`, or `npm run doc`; the `doc` script also runs the documentation tests. [package.json]
- Run style checks with `npm run style`, which combines the main, FP, performance, and test style checks. [package.json]
- Run the full validation workflow with `npm run validate`; it runs style checks followed by the test suite. [package.json]
- The browser CI workflow builds the project, starts a static server with `npx http-server -p 9001`, waits briefly, and then runs Playwright tests. [.github/workflows/browser-testing.yml]
- The visible browser-test port is `9001`. [test/playwright-runner.spec.js:5-8][test/backbone.html:9-18]
- The repository does not show a conventional application development server or a dedicated `start` script; the documented local browser workflow uses a static HTTP server after building. [package.json][.github/workflows/browser-testing.yml]

## Project Structure

- `lodash.js` contains the main generated JavaScript library and its internal helpers, wrappers, collection functions, and public utility methods. [lodash.js:1691-1749][lodash.js:9221-9273][lodash.js:14027-14029]
- `fp/` contains the functional-programming build support, including conversion logic and browser conversion helpers. [fp/_baseConvert.js:16-20][fp/_baseConvert.js:518-566][fp/_convertBrowser.js:11-13]
- `lib/common/` contains shared build utilities for copying, globbing templates, minification, writing files, error handling, and nested configuration objects. [lib/common/file.js:21-62][lib/common/util.js:15-35]
- `lib/main/` contains main-build modules for distribution files, documentation, module builds, and site generation. [lib/main/build-dist.js:24-29][lib/main/build-doc.js:63-81][lib/main/build-modules.js:27-32][lib/main/build-site.js:65-95]
- `lib/fp/` contains FP-specific distribution, documentation, and module-build logic. [lib/fp/build-dist.js:48-54][lib/fp/build-doc.js:30-36][lib/fp/build-modules.js:53-78]
- `test/` contains Node-based tests, browser QUnit suites, browser test assets, and Playwright runner tests. [package.json][test/index.html:1-18][test/fp.html:1-18][test/playwright-runner.spec.js:5-23]
- `doc/` contains generated API documentation for Lodash version `4.18.1`. [doc/README.md:1-6]
- `perf/` contains performance-related JavaScript utilities and benchmark support. [perf/perf.js:123-187]
- `vendor/` contains third-party assets and test dependencies, including JSON compatibility code, Underscore tests, and Firebug Lite sources. [test/backbone.html:14-18][test/underscore.html:369-407][vendor/json-js/json2.js:183-192][vendor/firebug-lite/src/firebug-lite-debug.js:593-593]
- `dist/` contains generated distribution files consumed by the FP browser test, and the CI workflow verifies that generated `dist/` files remain synchronized with source. [test/fp.html:10-12][.github/workflows/ci-dist-sync.yml]

## Testing

- The package defines separate main, FP, and documentation test commands: `npm run test:main`, `npm run test:fp`, and `npm run test:doc`. [package.json]
- Run the complete test suite with `npm test`; the package's `test` script runs both the main and FP tests, and `pretest` builds the project first. [package.json]
- Run all validation checks with `npm run validate`; this combines style checks and the complete test command. [package.json]
- The Node-based main test entry point is `test/test`, and the FP test entry point is `test/test-fp`. [package.json]
- The browser suites use QUnit, with pages at `test/index.html`, `test/fp.html`, `test/backbone.html`, and `test/underscore.html`. [test/index.html:1-18][test/fp.html:1-18][test/backbone.html:1-18][test/playwright-runner.spec.js:15-23]
- The browser pages load QUnit and `qunit-extras`, use `platform` for browser identification, and configure QUnit to run the corresponding suite. [test/index.html:13-18][test/fp.html:13-18][test/backbone.html:16-18]
- Browser tests exercise multiple builds and loaders through the shared `test/asset/test-ui.js` helper and page-specific loader configuration. [test/asset/test-ui.js:20-70][test/index.html:214-279][test/backbone.html:78-170]
- Playwright tests are defined in `test/playwright-runner.spec.js`; each test navigates to a browser suite on `http://localhost:9001` and expects visible `0 failed` output within 60 seconds. [test/playwright-runner.spec.js:5-23]
- Documentation tests use `markdown-doctest` against Markdown files under `doc/`. [package.json]
- CI runs validation under multiple Node.js versions, including versions `4` through `25`, and separately runs Playwright browser tests after building and starting the static server. [.github/workflows/ci-node.yml][.github/workflows/browser-testing.yml]
